h2: Radiographic testing in Seattle: licensing, pipelines, shipyards and fabrication
html:
Radiographic testing in Seattle: licensing, pipelines, shipyards and fabrication

Radiographic testing around Seattle is used on pipeline girth welds, coded vessel and spool fabrication, shipyard butt welds and castings. Washington is an NRC Agreement State, and industrial radiography there needs a radioactive-materials license from the Washington State Department of Health or a reciprocity approval. Atlantis, based in Houston, confirms the radiography arrangements for each job before it is scheduled.

How Washington controls radiography. Chapter 246-243 WAC sets the industrial radiography rules. Radiographers need classroom instruction, at least two months of on-the-job training and certification from a recognized certifying entity. Assistants need a written test and a practical examination. Licensees from other states work through the Department of Health's Office of Radiation Protection. Reciprocity requires 72 hours' notice each time work starts in the state and is valid for up to 180 days of work in a year. The application must include each radiographer's third-party certification. Atlantis does not claim to hold a particular license. The licensing route for each job is agreed in writing before the schedule is fixed.

Pipelines. Pipeline safety on intrastate gas and hazardous-liquid lines is enforced by the state Utilities and Transportation Commission. The commission also acts as lead inspector on interstate lines in the state, while PHMSA keeps enforcement. Operators on its list include Olympic Pipe Line, Williams' Northwest Pipeline and Puget Sound Energy. New construction and repair girth welds are radiographed to API 1104 under 49 CFR Part 192 or 195. In tight urban rights-of-way, the exclusion zone often decides the work window more than the weld count does.

Naval and commercial yards. Puget Sound Naval Shipyard in Bremerton and Vigor's Harbor Island yard both handle Navy repair. Radiography of piping and structural welds there is accepted against NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271, not a commercial code. Commercial new-build and steel renewal follow class rules. Waterfront yards are crowded, so radiography is usually done on night shifts or behind shielding to keep the controlled area small.

Fabrication and refinery work. Shops building ASME Section VIII vessels and B31.3 spools for the state's five refineries still use radiography as the reference record. Digital radiography shortens exposure times and stores images without film processing. Where the construction code allows ultrasonic examination in place of RT, TOFD or phased array avoid the exclusion zone entirely. That choice is settled in the procedure before mobilization.

  • Licensing: Washington Department of Health license or reciprocity under chapter 246-243 WAC
  • Pipeline girth welds to API 1104 for 49 CFR 192 and 195 operators
  • Naval welds and castings to NAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271
  • Vessel and spool fabrication to ASME Section VIII and B31.3
  • UT in place of RT where the code allows it

Next steps. The method and deliverables are described nationally on radiographic testing. Pipeline scopes in the city are on pipeline inspection in Seattle. For RT technician training, see radiographic testing training and the radiography simulator. Send the weld count, thicknesses and access constraints through the Seattle radiography enquiry.
